headline: Kerkering blows late lead, Phillies fall to Orioles 6-4
recap: The Phillies led Baltimore 4-2 through six innings behind six strong frames from Andrew Painter, who allowed two runs on three hits with six strikeouts and three walks. Reliever Orion Kerkering then surrendered four runs in two-thirds of an inning in the seventh, turning the two-run lead into a 6-4 Orioles win; he took the loss and blew his second save of the season. Trea Turner went 3-for-4 with a home run - his 16th of the year - and two runs scored, and J.T. Realmuto added a solo homer, his eighth. Baltimore's Pete Alonso finished 2-for-3 with a home run and two RBIs, and the go-ahead blow in the seventh was a two-run pinch-hit double from Christian Encarnacion-Strand.
The loss was Philadelphia's fourth straight, following a three-game sweep in Miami. The Phillies are 57-53, second in the NL East, 8 games behind the first-place Braves.

Philadelphia is back at Camden Yards tonight for game two of the series, with Cristopher Sanchez starting opposite Baltimore's Shane Baz. First pitch is scheduled for 7:05 PM ET. DraftKings has the Phillies as -144 favorites on the moneyline, with the Orioles at +119.
